title: memory-fragmentation-eviction-iterator-leak-oncall-notes
content:
Summary:

During a night-time traffic surge (2026-03-10 02:10-03:40 UTC) a subset of GPU hosts running the serving runtime experienced progressive memory growth culminating in OOMs on the host-level allocator and a cascade of request failures. Symptoms were distinct from previous KV-cache corruption incidents: process RSS was not showing large single-object allocations, but resident set grew steadily and GC-like free did not reclaim expected pages — indicative of heap fragmentation and live references held by an "eviction iterator" path.

Why this doc exists:
- On-call notes captured during triage.
- Initial hypothesis and quick mitigations recorded for follow-up.
- Draft runbook additions to help future responders detect and mitigate this class of regression quickly.

Observed signals (what alerted us):
- SLO alert: p95 generation latency > 700ms for serving-host pool A (03:02 UTC).
- Error budget burn: traffic-level 5xx increase from 0.3% to 4.8% in 20m.
- Host memory pressure alerts (host-level): free pages falling, fragmentation ratio metric high on 7 hosts.
- Prometheus metric "kv_cache.eviction_iterator_inflight" increased from <1 to ~120 across affected hosts.
- Grafana heap heatmap showed many small allocations (~512B-8KB) surviving for long durations.

Immediate on-call triage steps we performed:
1) Isolate traffic:
   - Shift traffic away from the affected availability zone via smart-routing (temporary region-fallback policy).
   - Scale up fallback replicas in Dedicated pool B for short-term capacity.
2) Collect diagnostics (preserve for postmortem):
   - Memory procmaps and jemalloc stats saved from 5 representative hosts to /tmp/incident-dumps/INF-3042/ (ticket link).
   - Heap profiles (tcmalloc/jemalloc) and ltrace/callstack captures for in-flight eviction iterations.
   - KV cache internal metrics snapshot (prefetch queue length, eviction iterator counts, compaction last-run timestamp).
3) Quick mitigations tried:
   - Disable aggressive prefetching on the affected config (flag: --prefetch-enabled=false). Immediate effect: drop in new iterator creation but existing iterator count slowly decremented.
   - Restarted the runtime process on two most-pressured hosts (rolling restart). Those hosts dropped RSS by ~18% after restart and resumed serving normally.
   - Activated conservative batching policy to reduce churn of small allocations (reduced microbatch churn).

Initial hypothesis (why it happened):
- A change in PR #1987 altered the eviction iterator lifecycle: iterator objects now hold a small per-request allocation buffer until iterator completion. Under high continuous-batching churn the iterator completion path was raced/polled less frequently, so many iterator objects stuck alive and prevented page coalescing by the allocator.
- Interaction with allocator (jemalloc) + GPU host memory allocator caused fragmentation: many small live objects scattered across arenas prevented large free spans, causing overall RSS to creep up even though total logical free memory was high.
- Compaction/GC not triggered because the runtime's compaction heuristics expect different allocation patterns; the regression created many small long-lived objects rather than fewer medium-lived ones.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- Heap profiles show increased count of a site labeled eviction_iterator::node (stack traces point to serving-runtime/src/kv/eviction.cc:line ~412).
- The compaction task last-run timestamp was stale on affected hosts; enabling compaction manually reduced fragmentation on one host (experiment).
- Synthetics that reproduce high microbatch churn increased iterator_inflight and slowly raised RSS in local repro.

Why this is different from previous KV-cache incidents:
- Not a corruption or index-mismatch. Keys remained consistent; responses were correct until host-level OOM.
- Failure mode was slow progressive RSS growth (fragmentation) rather than sudden invalidation or data loss.

Short-term mitigations recommended (for on-call runbook):
- Detection: add an alert for kv_cache.eviction_iterator_inflight > 50 sustained for 10m AND host_fragmentation_ratio > 0.45.
- Rapid response: toggle --prefetch-enabled=false; switch to conservative batch policy; roll one host at a time if RSS > 85% and fragmentation ratio > 0.5.
- Preserve diagnostics before restart: heap profile, jemalloc stats, /proc/<pid>/smaps.

Draft runbook steps (to be added to serving-runtime incident playbook):
1) Alert hit -> pager duty -> SRE oncall responds.
2) Immediately check Grafana panels: eviction iterator, compaction last-run, fragmentation ratio, host RSS.
3) If iterator_inflight spike present: apply toggle to config: feature.prefetch=false and batch.policy=conservative.
4) If RSS still climbs after 10m -> perform rolling restart on worst hosts (one every 3 minutes).
5) Once stable, capture heap/profiles and file ticket with reproducible scenario (link to INF-3042).

Longer term action items (owners and rough ETA):
- ENG-SRV-210 (Diego): revert iterator lifecycle change or add deterministic finalizer; ETA 2 weeks.
- ENG-ALLOC-34 (Marta): tune compaction heuristics to trigger on fragmentation pattern; ETA 3 weeks.
- SRE: add alert and dashboard panels for fragmentation ratio and iterator leak signal; ETA 3 days (owner: Ravi).
- QA/Perf: add microbatch churn scenarios in the nightly perf harness to detect similar regressions; ETA 2 weeks (owner: Asha).
- Infra: document safe rollback steps for private clusters (owner: Liam); ETA 1 week.

Notes / open questions:
- Is the iterator object holding GPU pinned memory indirectly (via a host-side pinned buffer)? Need to validate with lower-level GPU allocator traces.
- Why did compaction not run? Is compaction backoff logic suppressed under high load?
- Should we expose a manual compaction endpoint for emergency use?

Appendix: useful commands captured during triage
- Collect jemalloc stats: curl -s localhost:9001/debug/je_stats > /tmp/JE-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).txt
- Heap profile (production): kill -SIGABRT <pid> to force heap dump (followed existing ops policy); saved to S3 bucket s3://infra-dumps/INF-3042/
- Check iterator counts: curl -s localhost:9001/metrics | grep eviction_iterator_inflight

Slack threads / tickets to follow: #inc-eviction-iterator (Slack), INF-3042 (Jira), PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1987 (possible regression).

Immediate status (as of 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC):
- Traffic normalized after region fallback and rolling restarts.
- No further OOMs observed for 36 hours on affected pools.
- Draft runbook steps created; awaiting review and merge.

If you're taking this on-call next: focus on the iterator count signal first, don't assume it's KV corruption. Save profiles before restarting; restarts solve symptoms but lose transient debugging data.

End of notes.
